newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Shipley to repeat NZ argument for beyond rights.
newsitem.headline: Shipley to repeat NZ argument for beyond rights.

text.p: Transport Minister Jenny Shipley will be the latest in a string of New Zealand government representatives to try to convince Australia to grant beyond rights for Air New Zealand when she meets her Australian counterpart John Sharp on Friday, the New Zealand Press Association reported on Thursday.
New to the transport portfolio, Shipley will meet the slightly more seasoned Sharp, who was appointed Australia's minister of transport almost a year ago.
The two will hold private talks before taking part in the annual Australasian transport ministers meeting.
Beyond rights would enable Air New Zealand to pass through Australia, collecting more passengers and flying on to other overseas destinations.
Existing arrangements allow Air New Zealand to fly the equivalent of 12 747s out of Australia to North America and Asian markets, but New Zealand is seeking more extensive access.
The rights were included in the initial agreement for a single aviation market unilaterally cancelled by former Australian prime minister Paul Keating.
The single market signed last year allows Australian airlines to fly domestically within New Zealand and vice versa, but despite strong urgings from New Zealand, did not include beyond rights.

The present Australian government, in opposition at that time, was critical of the Keating administration's handling of the affair and New Zealand has tried to use that criticism as a moral lever on the John Howard-led coalition.

In spite of former transport minister Maurice Williamson's optimism that the issue was virtually resolved shortly before the October 2 election, it is understood New Zealand has yet to convince the Australian government of benefits for Australia in granting the rights.

NZPA understands New Zealand's case is not being helped by a claim from Australian government representatives that Air New Zealand is not using its full allocation of the limited rights it already has.

New Zealand government officials have argued Australia would gain from the increased competition a greater Air New Zealand presence would bring. But while Sharp himself might embrace the concept of across-the-board competition, he has to convince his Australian cabinet colleagues of the benefits.
Shipley returns to New Zealand following the meeting on Friday.
